name: Re-belle
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading, cut to Hall of Femme's
design. Everything that makes it a Snapchat pack is Hall of Femme's
and comes from the same two presets rather than being restated here:
the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the transcription, the
rewrite that turns speech into report, the stated 40px, the twenty
characters to a line, the freeform text box, the drag.
What makes it this show rather than that one is the face and the
colours: it is set in a signature hand with picked words in Syne
Bold, in a purple, a white, a pink and a red the user pairs between
the type and the card. Each is argued where it is stated.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the pack it was cut from. Hall of
Femme sets its captions in Telegraf - a 200-weight hairline for the
block, the 800 for a picked word - on a hot pink card, in sixteen
pairings the user chooses between. This one is set in Brittany
Signature, a joined signature hand, with picked words in Syne Bold,
in a purple, a white, a pink or a red the user pairs per frame, on a
card.
The face is what the rest is in service of, and that has not
changed. It is why `uppercase` is off and why the highlight is a
change of kind of writing rather than of colour.
The card has. This pack used to argue that a card under a signature
turns it into a label, and set the caption on the photograph with a
white halo. The show has since asked for colours for the letters AND
for a ground behind them, which is a request for a card - the panel
palette cannot exist without one (see editor.paletteOf). So it is on
the card its carded siblings use, and what follows from that is
written once, in content/README.md, under 'A channel that set its
caption on the photograph may take the card back'. The label
argument is now the show's to weigh per frame: the white card is the
quietest ground of the four, and the closest to the paper a
signature is written on.

_comment_uppercase: Off, and this pack is the second under the Snapchat heading where
it is - Killer Bites is the other, and its note is worth reading
beside this one because the reasons are different.
The preset's argument for capitals is that at 40px with twenty
characters to a line a caption is three short beats rather than a
paragraph, and beats are what capitals are for. That argument is
about grotesques. This face is a signature hand, and a signature
hand has no capitals in the sense the preset means: its letters
are drawn to JOIN, and the joins live in the lower case. Set in
capitals it comes apart into twenty unconnected swash initials -
not a louder version of the same hand but a different and much
harder-to-read object, and the one thing that made it worth
choosing is gone.
It is applied at the draw and not to what is stored, so turning
it off changes only what the canvas does: the text box held the
user's own casing all along, and the highlight buttons already
offered the words as the canvas would set them (see the `cased`
note in js/text.js and editor.renderWordButtons).
It reaches the picked words too - `uppercase` is the block's and
there is one of it - so Syne Bold is set in lower case as well.
That is the right answer for the same reason at one remove: what
separates a picked word here is that it is suddenly a typeface
instead of a hand, and it does not need a second difference
stacked on top of it.
_comment_color: The show's purple, and the channel's own answer: what every frame
is set in until somebody presses a swatch, since a frame stores no
colour of its own until it is given one (see state.textColorFor).
It opens the list in `colors` below, so the purple swatch is the
one shown as chosen on an untouched frame.
It is also the colour of a picked word - see `highlight` - which
makes it the colour of the whole caption, and whichever swatch the
user presses keeps it that way. That is the deliberate half of
what makes this show read as handwriting: a signature is written
in one ink, and a caption in two colours would be a graphic rather
_comment_colors: The show's purple, then the white, the pink and the red it asked
for, offered for the letters and for the card behind them - four
buttons each in the title panel (see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same four in both lists and in one order, which is what Hall
of Femme does and for its reason: the point is the PAIRING. Purple
on white is what the show opens on; white on pink and white on red
are the loud ones, a button away.
Nothing stops the user setting purple on purple. The two lists are
independent because the pairing is the feature, and the user can
see the caption has gone and presses another swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note
on `colors` in js/channels.js - which is what keeps the caption in
one ink whatever is picked (see `color` above).
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Syne Bold, in the same purple as the rest
of the block. This is Hall of Femme's highlight exactly - the
colour is stated and it is the block's, so the recolour draws
what its neighbours are drawn in and the FACE is the whole of the
difference - with the one change that the two faces here are not
two cuts of a family but two different kinds of writing.
A bold grotesque in the middle of a signature hand is the loudest
change two words can make without changing colour, and it makes
it at a glance on a phone - which is why it never needed to become
a box, on the photograph or on the card.
Colour mode and word scope are the preset's, and the argument for
picking out words rather than lines lives there: a caption's line
breaks are wherever the sentence ran out of width, so picking a
LINE out picks out a fragment rather than a thought.
No shadow of its own any more. The white halo it used to restate
was there to match the block's on the photograph; with the card
back, the preset's null is right for both (see content/README.md).
_comment_panel: White, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are
the Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
White because it is the first colour the show asked for, the
purple reads on it at once, and it is the ground closest to the
paper a signature is written on (see `_comment_title`). The pink
and the red are the other cards a button away.
